This VCA Hospital is not a veterinary hospital where you want to take your pet.  Our experience was awful.  Unfortunately, what we saw and experienced was all about money and how much they could charge, not about the care of your pet.  We witnessed the front desk instructing pet owners on where they could take their sick pets to a nearby vet, which would cost less than the estimate VCA provided when the owners indicated they could not afford the estimate.  When the neurologists were discussing our pet's condition, they pushed to keep her another night, even though they did not know what was wrong with her, so they could “monitor” her.  Once we indicated we wanted to take her home, you could see the change and disengagement from the conversation when he realized VCA was not going to make additional money from us. Soon after that, he left the room, and we never spoke to the head of neurology again.  Our pet left VCA in worse condition than when we brought her in. We 100% believe they missed her condition, Cushing’s Syndrome which, if caught earlier, there are treatments for.  This led us to euthanize our pet.  We called VCA and had a conversation with the Specialty Department Manager, who said she would relate our concerns to her team, discuss and call me back.  This callback, of course, never happened.

Update 10/8/26:
We recently had the 1-year anniversary of the passing of our dog Olive.  I thought this was a good time to reiterate and hopefully warn others not to take their pet to VCA Animal Specialty Group unless they want to pay a lot of money and get poor care.  A month after I wrote my original Google review, VCA responded with their “canned response” (see below).  The reason I say it's canned is that I was clear in my review that we already had several conversations with VCA before and after our pet passed away about our feelings on the treatment Olive received and how we felt we were treated, as an ATM, not about the care of the pet.  In their response; “we would appreciate the opportunity to speak with you directly to understand better what happened and explore how we might help bring clarity or closure.” Clearly, they did not read my original review or even discuss it internally with the people we spoke to before dropping their response to our review.  We were very clear with them and they knew exactly how we felt and why.  This is just another item in the list of things that show their lack of real understanding or concern about the pet or their owners.

I am very very frustrated with VCA. A few weeks back, we met with their Neurologist and she was absolutely wonderful. However, we decided to do his lab work and urine sample. They provided us a quote And We brought him in for the tests. When we were checking out, I brought to their attention that what we were being charged was far less than what we were quoted and they told us that it’s just a happy accident. when we got home, we were called and asked to pay the remaining balance Because they had made a mistake when they charged us. 3 days later received a call that they did not collect enough urine. Mind you we live one hour away and we had to drive back down to give a second urine sample today. The assistant vet found blood in his urine while collecting the same and when we asked what we should do about that or if that’s a concern, she told us that we need to Call the office and ask to speak with the Neurologist. That does not seem like the best solution given the fact that we were already in an emergency hospital. We drove an hour back home and then called the neurologist. We left a message with reception that our cat has blood in his urine and we need to know if this is an emergency or if we need to take him To an emergency vet. Additionally, he is supposed to begin his treatment for FIP tonight, prescribed by their clinic. When we called the office, they told us it will take 24 to 48 hours for us to get a call Back from the vet. They also told us that if we were concerned that we can bring him back to the vet to be seen… We had just left and they had just told us to go home and call the vet! We have no idea if we are allowed to begin his treatment or not. This is ridiculous! They informed us that there was Blood in our cats urine, but aren’t giving us any guidance on if we need to take him to an emergency vet or if we need to not start his treatment. Although the neurologist Is a wonderful vet, the communication system and lack of urgency during emergency situations is very concerning. My partner and I feel very confused, concerned, and have no idea what the next best step is. If you are in any sort of rush, I would never recommend this vet. It’s truly unfortunate because the neurologist are Very talented and knowledgeable however, the rest of the office staff has made the experience Very stressful and confusing.
The staff care and diagnosis of my dog Ash  were excellent

Everyone treated our pup and us with such kindness and communicated very clearly with us about his TPLO surgery and the recovery process. We are so happy with our decision to have Dr. Wendelburg preform the surgery and how caring the staff has been with our pup.

Everyone at the VCA handled our dogs TPLO surgery process with so much care.

Thank you VCA for your compassion. We brought our 17 year old cat in after she started peeing blood.

They found a mass on her bladder and we made the very hard decision to let her go.

They made the process as easy as possible.

There are truly no words that can fully express how grateful I am to Dr. Kim and the entire team at VCA for saving my dog’s life.

My dog had ingested a foreign object and underwent emergency surgery at another hospital. In the days following that surgery, instead of recovering, he became critically ill. By the time I transferred him to VCA, he was septic, his incision sites were leaking, and his condition had deteriorated to the point that we were genuinely at risk of losing him.

Dr. Kim and her team recognized the severity of the situation immediately and rushed him into a second emergency surgery. I truly believe that if it were not for Dr. Kim’s skill, judgment, and determination that day, my dog would not be here today. She didn’t just perform a surgery, she saved his life.

What I will never forget, though, is that Dr. Kim also advocated for him. After seeing the condition he was in and the complications from his previous surgery, she personally contacted the medical director of the other hospital to address her concerns about the care he had received. At that point, I was so physically and emotionally exhausted from watching my dog fight for his life that I did not have the strength to advocate the way I normally would have. Dr. Kim stepped in and did that for us. Knowing that someone was not only fighting to save my dog medically, but was also willing to stand up for him, meant more to me than I can put into words.

I also want to thank Dr. DeNezzo, who helped us during our initial emergency intake at VCA and helped get us through those terrifying first moments, as well as Dr. Mannucci and every doctor, nurse, technician, and staff member who cared for my dog throughout his stay. During one of the worst experiences of my life, I knew he was surrounded by people who were doing everything possible to give him a chance.

Because of Dr. Kim and this incredible team, I still have my dog with me today. I will never forget what they did for him or for me. Thank you, Dr. Kim, for saving his life, for advocating for him when I couldn’t, and for treating him like a life worth fighting for. I will be grateful to you and your team for the rest of my life.

My 18-year-old cat, Hobbes, was a patient here from September 2024 until his passing in July 2025.

During his final hospitalization (June 30 – July 2, 2025), I was told a procedure to relieve his constipation was futile, and euthanasia was presented as the first option. I transferred him to his primary care veterinarian, who performed that procedure the same afternoon. When we returned to the ER that night, one doctor, Dr. Max Gluck, finally laid out the full range of options with honesty and compassion. By then Hobbes had deteriorated, and we let him go.

Earlier, I was told to "be realistic about trying to keep him alive." His internist never contacted us after he passed.

The front desk staff were kind. But if you have a senior or chronically ill pet, ask for every option in writing, and get a second opinion before accepting that nothing more can be done.

Everyone that interacted with my dog and I, you all made a huge difference in how I was able to make peace with saying goodbye to my beloved fur son, Scud.

Letting go of a long time pet is hard, but the dignity my dog passed with could not have happened with the extreme kindness of the VCA staff. You guys made a difficult , emotional situation much more manageable, and I will forever be grateful.

The vet tech..forgot her name...she was amazing

It was seamless and pleasant as it could be
Yes, they tried everything but my boy was put down on Friday afternoon and it was so painful 😒 …

‼️🚫 SCAM ALERT  - STAY AWAY 🚫‼️
WORST EXPERIENCE OF MY LIFE

The front desk staff were extremely rude, dismissive, unprofessional, and focused heavily on payment and their lunch rather than my dog.
The wait was over 8 hours, communication was non existent, and I had to repeatedly push for updates. The level of urgency and professionalism was nowhere near what I expect from an VCA facility, and the final bill was double the initial estimate. When your pet’s health and safety are on the line, this is not a risk I would take. For a ANY  emergency or vet needs, go anywhere elsewhere. Plus the whole place reeks of sewage. A serious health concern. 🚫‼️

Surgery team is amazing. Dr. Hubert, Sarah and Dr. Davie were so communicative and helpful!

Amazing service, communication, and empathy.

My miniature dachshund Slinky had to have emergency back surgery.

Dr. Kwan and Dr. Barry have been amazing during the entire process. Thank you so much for all that you do. The whole process was scary but they ensured to keep me updated every step of the way.

I had a great experience with everyone at the facility. All my questions were answered.

Having staff members get friends and family to leave fake 5 star Google reviews to boost your score and try and cover up all the real, truthful, reviews from real paying customers; isn’t helping anyone.
You guys should be shut down. The sanitation issue alone should be enough.
These people are money hungry who don’t care about you or your animal and would charge you for the air in the waiting room if they could.
The stuff is rude and the doctors so inexperienced it’s scary. Save your money, your animal, and your sense of smell and go somewhere/ anywhere else.

The entire front office staff can't remember names, but all the girls are very professional

Doctor Ohashi was very professional and compassionate, and she explained everything in detail. After the visit, Tigrina started feeling better.

Love everyone at the clinic!!!

You guys are amazing!

I honestly cannot say enough good things about VCA Emergency and the entire team who took care of my Bigxby.

From the moment we arrived, after being ref. by our primary veterinarian for an emergency, I was immediately impressed by how attentive, organized, and compassionate everyone was. The hospital is clearly structured w/ different departments and specialists working together, which gave me so much confidence that my dog was in the right hands.

Bigxby needed an emergency surgery a "hemilaminectomy" and today marks 6 weeks since her post-surgery re assessment. Her surgery was performed by Dr. Kwan and his surgical team and me and my significant other will forever be grateful for the care they provided. Bigxby is now back to walking and almost normal. Feed back is positive.

One of the things that meant the most to me was how consistently they kept me updated throughout the entire process. From the moment she went into surgery, during the procedure, and afterward, they made sure I knew what was happening. When you're sitting there worried about your fur baby, those updates mean everything. They helped keep me calm and gave me peace of mind knowing that she was being carefully monitored and cared for.

I was also very impressed by how clean, neat, and organized the facility was. But beyond the physical environment, it was the people who truly made the experience special. Every staff member I encountered was attentive, professional, and genuinely caring.

Looking back, I am so grateful that our primary vet referred us to VCA Emergency and that we chose to have Bigxby treated there. Emergency surgery is something no pet parent ever wants to go through, but having a team that communicates, stays attentive, and treats your pet with such care makes an incredibly difficult situation a little easier.

6 weeks later, seeing Bigxby continuing on her recovery journey makes me even more thankful to Dr. Kwan, his associates, and everyone at VCA Emergency who helped care for her and to others.
Continue to work w/ passion.

I brought my dog here after he suffered a serious, traumatic injury because I trusted VCA to treat him properly. What followed was one of the most disturbing veterinary experiences I have ever had.
Before my dog could even be seen by a doctor, I was required to pay a $700 deposit. He was taken to the back almost immediately, but I then waited nearly four hours before finally speaking face-to-face with the doctor and her assistant. They explained the treatment plan: repair his wound with stitches, clean him up, give him pain medication, and discharge him. I was told it would take another 4–5 hours, so I eventually left to get something to eat.
Approximately three hours after that consultation, the doctor called me while I was out and asked what ointment I had put on my dog’s wound.
I explained that before bringing him in, I had applied a pet-safe antiseptic wound ointment specifically intended for open wounds and bleeding, purchased at Petco, and wrapped the wound with pet-safe gauze and bandages, also purchased at Petco. I did this to control the active bleeding and protect the wound from contamination until he could receive veterinary treatment.
I was then told the ointment had supposedly “dried out” the wound and that my dog would now require an additional procedure costing nearly twice what I was originally quoted…

So, if the doctor was calling me nearly eight hours after I brought my dog in, to ask me what ointment had been applied to his wound.. then that means that this was the very time that his wound was actually examined by the doctor.
Had it been looked at earlier, the doctor would have definitely asked about the ointment during our face to face consultation nearly 3 hours prior.

That means my dog spent approximately eight hours in a hot, smelly, cage with a serious open wound while I was being given a treatment plan for an injury that had not even been looked at yet.
Not okay.
But they had already taken my $700 deposit and were already billing me for treatment?
What’s even more concerning , I was then told that my efforts to responsibly control the bleeding and protect the wound had supposedly contributed to the problem. No. If the wound became more difficult to close because it had begun healing during those eight hours, that is precisely the kind of issue that might have been avoided had it been properly examined and treated earlier. I will not accept responsibility for protecting my injured dog before bringing him to a veterinary hospital.
The original estimate and final charges were dramatically different. I ultimately faced more than $2,000 in charges, including nearly $2,000 for the wound repair/stitches, despite initially being quoted substantially less. The entire ordeal—from arrival to discharge—lasted approximately 13 hours.
Then came the prescriptions.
I was given three prescriptions costing more than $200 total. One contained only three pills and cost $56—$18.67 per pill. When I questioned the price, I was told it was because of their “dispensing fee.” By then it was nearly 11 PM, after I had spent essentially the entire day at the hospital, leaving me with no practical opportunity to shop around for another pharmacy.
Staff were rude and appeared more concerned with how and when I was going to pay than with my dog. Employees were eating food and on their phones, and the entire clinic—inside and outside—smelled like sulfur and something rotting. It was disgusting. The doctor was dismissive, and throughout this ordeal I felt like I had to fight for basic answers about what was happening to my dog and why the treatment plan and cost kept changing.
What bothers me most is not simply the money. It is that I no longer have confidence in what actually happened to my dog while he was in their care.
I intend to file a complaint with the appropriate veterinary regulatory authorities.
My dog is my family—not a customer number, an invoice, or a revenue opportunity.
VCA Glendale needs to do much better.
My advice: DO YOUR RESEARCH AND CONSIDER OTHER OPTIONS.

VCA abused a famous Los Angeles hospital therapy dog. Horrible cruelty!My French Bulldog, Petunia, is a famous dog in Los Angeles with her own popular YouTube channel. She spends her life volunteering in LA hospitals, bringing comfort and joy to sick children. What VCA did to her is completely wrong and unacceptable.After standard shots, she started actively bleeding and suffocating on the way home [image_v-PyCT.png]. I rushed her back, but VCA made a critically ill, suffocating dog sit in the lobby for TWO HOURS without triage. For two days, they harassed us with threats to stop life-saving treatments [image_TImJWP.png]. When we initiated a transfer, they panicked, wrote fraudulent lies in her paperwork, and listed a doctor I was never allowed to speak with [image_ENs36d.png, image_v-PyCT.png].They returned Petunia to us deeply traumatized, shaking, with an aggressively shaved rear and a severely swollen, inflamed vulva. They even shaved a heart into her fur for no medical reason, treating a sick therapy dog like a joke. When I asked to speak to a doctor to ensure she was safe to travel, they threw her papers in my face and forced us out.Petunia has been transferred to another hospital, and we are praying for her. VCA abuses pets, extorts owners, and fakes documents to cover up negligence. We are taking very serious legal action under California law.

Everyone is terrific. I especially appreciate Drs. Collins, Meng, and Ohashi

Everyone is really great...I wish VCA ASG were a little less expensive, but they really take good care of furry loved ones.

Also, if your little buddy needs surgery and stays several days at the hospital, you are more than welcome to visit. I think this is pretty rare for veterinarian hospitals.

Our experience with VCA Animal Specialty Group was truly wonderful.When Benji needed surgery, we were understandably worried and emotional, but the entire team treated him with so much kindness, patience, and compassion. They took the time to explain everything clearly, answer all of our questions, and reassure us throughout the process, We never felt like just another patient — we felt that Benji was genuinely cared for and that his well being mattered to everyone. We are incredibly grateful to Dr Huber and the entire team for taking such good care of our boy. Thank you  for everything.

Both Dr Collins and the staff member who debriefed me at the end of his visit were exceptionally thorough, patient, and communicative. All of my concerns were heeded and my questions answered. A great experience (especially during an anxious time).

Swift, conscientious, thorough, and respectful. I had a great experience and will be sure to bring my cat back if/when a similar medical issue with him arises. Great to know he's in good hands!

We came to VCASG this past Sunday for an emergency with my 1 year old cavapoo. We were sent by his primary as he needed an ultrasound to figure out if he had severe pancreatitis or a possible obstruction.

I was nervous coming here as the only ER vet I’ve ever had to go to was Blue Pearl in Irvine (who are absolutely incredible, but we couldn’t risk his health for the drive). Here in LA I don’t feel that you can read reviews and feel super confident in the ER vets we have around here.

I’m writing this review on my experience as I know it may help ease the mind of other pet owners. Upon first walking in I was worried because it just felt quiet between staff / the appearance of the waiting room felt slightly uninviting. Eventually after more communication I realized the staff is all very friendly just very busy.

Our ER doctor (will grab his name and edit later) was extremely upbeat and knowledgeable and gave us an incredible amount of information about how they were going to test and treat Frankie. We were given possibilities of each treatment depending on whether it was pancreatitis or an obstruction. We left feeling comfortable about the hands he was being left in.

He later called to inform us of the bad news that they found a shadow in Frankie’s intestines indicating an obstruction and that they were opting for exploratory surgery. We agreed.

Later we received a call from Dr. Safari on the surgical team. She was very thorough in the information she gave us leading us to the best decision as to when to do the surgery. After the surgery she did the same and gave us such amazing, clear, & helpful information.

After the surgery he was passed onto Dr. Lynn for post op care. She was also incredible answering any questions and giving us so much information. She called me to give great updates twice a day. After he was discharged I still had more questions and concerns - being anxious with how high risk his surgery was and I was met with such kindness while she answered my questions. I was glad to not feel like an annoying pet owner. She even let me know that I could email them photos for them to check to ease my mind.

The whole experience was as pleasant as one like this could be. I’m really happy with the pre and post op care he has received and I’m incredibly grateful.

Pricing - all vet care is expensive ER or primary. I highly suggest health insurance for this reason - my former dog didn’t have it and I lost approx $20k on his heart failure treatment and hospitalizations. I felt VCASG actually had incredibly reasonable pricing for all of the care and quality of care he received. He was there from Sunday around 1 pm until Wednesday at 530 pm and I was shocked at how low his bill was.

Blue Pearl in Irvine would have been much more expensive (but totally worth it) and VCASG is also worth every penny, definitely an extra relief with their pricing. These are the only two ER vets that i trust in LA and OC. I hope this helps anyone else who may need care in either of these areas.

They traumatized my sisters dog, came for nausea, vomiting and internal bleeding, they throw them out because my sister wanted answers from doctor, never see any. Bills are huge, never explained what they did to the dog. The dog is in a critical condition with spine fracture from Hospital, traumatized, not moving.
All family is crying, in distress what they did to so lovely baby.
PLEASE BE AWARE THAT HOSPITAL IS DANGER FOR YOUR ANIMALS

Nothing says I love you like money. Kept my cat here cause she had trouble breathing. Costs daily $1000. Then $1800 later n broke .. suddenly they say I needed to pick up my cat pronto and that she was fine now

From the moment I arrived, the entire staff was welcoming, professional, and compassionate. They treated my pet with such kindness and care and took the time to explain everything clearly, answer my questions, and make sure I felt comfortable with the treatment plan.

It was obvious that everyone genuinely cares about the animals they treat. The veterinarian was knowledgeable, thorough, and incredibly attentive, and the staff made what could have been a stressful visit feel calm and reassuring.

I am extremely grateful for the excellent care my pet received and would highly recommend this veterinary hospital to anyone looking for a compassionate, knowledgeable, and trustworthy team. Thank you for such a wonderful experience!
Dr. Sengewald (Neurology) is incredibly caring & patient, answered all our questions and is clearly very knowledgeable & skilled. 10/10 the emergency vet every pet parent should have on speed dial

Emma and Mary were both so comforting and encouraging throughout this process. Also the front desk staff was incredibly welcoming and attentive despite being extremely busy every appointment I brought Buster in for.

I was so incredibly worried when I came in after being told by another vet that it was likely Buster's tail wound would require surgery and possible amputation. The doctors were so calming and friendly and immediately put my mind at ease. I felt very comfortable expressing my concerns and asking questions and am so happy they were able to right away assess that the wound was not as big a cause for concern as the other vet had led me to blieve.

Roni and I forgot the man’s name who leashed Oliver and brought him up to the front. They were funny and it’s always nice hearing people say how much they loved my dog and gave him love while in the back away from me.

The whole oncology staff was so kind to my husband and myself but even more so to my dog Oliver. Their compassion and care was clearly visible.

I brought my Doberman to this emergency animal hospital after repeated vomiting, diarrhea and obvious discomfort, after waiting nearly an hour, I was told the wait could be another 8 hours.
I understand triage, what I don’t understand is this level of unprofessionalism from an emergency hospital. My dog is reactive so I responsibly muzzled him for everyone’s safety. Because he was already sick and the muzzle made him even more uncomfortable, I took him outside to wait. When he started gagging, I called concerned about his condition, Instead of asking about his symptoms or reassessing him, I was told “We don’t appreciate your tone.” And when I said I didn’t appreciate their unprofessionalism they hung up on me while I was outside with my sick dog.

This is the second time this has happened, I previously rushed my other Doberman here after she ingested grapes she wasn’t seen either and I had to rush her to another emergency hospital to actually get treatment.

The facility itself is also extremely dirty with strong smells of feces and urine, along with a very strong swear smell completely unacceptable for an animal hospital.

Two dogs. Two emergencies. Same experience.
And please spare people the generic apologies under negative reviews. People don’t need apologies after the fact they need you to address the problems they keep complaining about. If the wait is 8 hours, tell people immediately so they can take their sick animal somewhere that can actually see them.

Given the horrible nature of my visit, having to say goodbye to my 15 year old chihuahua, VCA Animal Specialty Group made the experience as peaceful and smooth as possible. I had already scheduled an at home euthanasia appt for my sweet girl for the next day, but that night things escalated, and I knew it was time, and couldn't wait until the next day. I called the office on my way over and explained my situation, and although it was late Saturday night, 4th of July, and quite busy in the lobby, they took me to a room right away once I arrived. They were very good about explaining everything to me, and giving me options for her aftercare. The process was quick and peaceful. I came back a couple weeks later to pick up her ashes, and was so pleased with how beautifully everything was wrapped up and tucked into a little bag. I am grateful for them, having made such a sad and painful experience a little bit easier💖

Dr. Schulman is an absolute rockstar. She is clearly knowledgable about the possible treatment choices for my cat's distress and treated both of us with respect and dignity. She should be recognized as a leader in this field, both because of her knowledge and skill and her bedside manner. I could trust that, when my cat and I entered the office, Dr. Schulman would advocate for us and provide us with the best possible care. I cannot thank her enough.

During the last year I have felt respected as a client and pet owner. I was well taken care of by all of the doctors and staff at VCA and would recommend the internal medicine team to any of my friends or family.
Dr Oliphant is amazing as well as the entire Neurology staff.
My cat Sukihana was in good hands here!

My doggie Mookie was nearly 18 and started not feeling so well. I took him to VCA ASP from Media City Vet recommendation (our usual vet) because they were only doing surgeries in the early morning.
Sadly at the VCA, I found out my baby had chronic kidney disease, some mass on the lungs and a lot of ailments from old age. He’s always been so active and never shown any sickness until the end so the decline was fast. Dr. Boyajian was the emergency vet and had to break all this devastating news to me. She was very gentle with the info though still very hard to take. She suggested I take him home and spend finals days loving him. He died 3 days later. I brought him back to VCA on July 4th morning. Ashley was super sweet and helpful letting us walk our final walk with him. Full circle where we found out he was sick to his final resting place. I’m grateful the VCA was more than just an animal hospital but understood how our pets are our family and showed sympathy and sensitivity during a most difficult time. It’s been nearly two weeks and I’ve just received a card of condolence and grief counseling recommendation from the VCA. Thank you. 🙏

Everyone was extremely helpful and caring, and our doctor (Dr Huber, if I recall correctly) was absolutely amazing... He explained everything so thoroughly and answered any of the questions that we had.

Even though this hospital deals with higher quantities of pet patients than my local veterinarian's office, it did not feel like we were being rushed through, nor did it feel like my dog's care and importance ever dropped... Overall, they were very professional and caring.

My dog, Puppa, was diagnosed with an auto-immune disease in February. Since then, we have been back to this hospital multiple times for her visits, as this is the closest hospital to us with a veterinary neurologist.

This hospital, in my humble opinion, has been such a lifesaver. My dog's condition is serious. I could not afford certain tests. They assured me they would not let me walk away without some kind of treatment for my baby. While I was not able to afford certain tests, we did begin treatment on an assumed diagnosis, and she has been doing AMAZING since. We have to go get her checked out every few months, but the staff (both the front desk staff, vet tech, vets) are all amazing. They have treated me and my dog with nothing but kindness, empathy, and patience since becoming a patient at this clinic.

When I call with any concerns or to reorder medication, there is rarely a hold time. The people I speak to are very friendly and kind, as are the doctors when I call in with a questions. It is very anxiety-inducing and saddening when a pet is diagnosed with a chronic medical illness, but the Veterinarians have been so patient, kind, empathetic, and willing to answer any question I have had. Special shout out to Dr. Kwan, my baby's neurologist!

This is kind of unrelated to the care, but they have free candy, coffee, and accessories (like a dog leash) for owners. I find this comforting. It sucks going to the vet, and even as an adult, it's nice to have candy to make me feel better. To me, it's an additional little detail that means a lot, as it shows that they recognize this experience is hard on the owners as well.

I am thankful to everyone at this particular location. Thank you all, not only for your commitment to some of the most vulnerable members of our community, but for being so kind and understanding during what is a difficult visit for many pet owners. Words cannot express how much I truly appreciate everyone at this facility who has been a part of our journey!

Thank you Dr. Dana Sengewald, DVM, DACVIM, Neurologist for the caring, thorough, comprehensive exam of our pug with neurological issues.  We were so grateful for the outstanding care, the lack of wait time, the extremely reasonable cost for the exam, that we frankly expected to be much more expensive, and for the honesty and lack of pressure to do more than what was truly needed.From the time of her diagnosis ten years ago, to this third periodic checkup, we have always had an exceptional experience at this specialty vet group.

FOREVER TRAUMATIZED BY DR. OHASHI & TEAM

I'm here to echo the MANY traumatic experiences from people who were seen by Dr. Ohashi - the primary oncologist at VCA and truly an evil human being. A negative experience that not only negligently left our dog PARALYZED in his final days but also spending unnecessary money on a treatment that would not benefit him. It's truly unbelievable that this horrid woman still maintains a job let alone a client facing role in this hospital.

I brought my sweet boy Obi in urgently after an unexpected and gruesome cancer diagnosis that we received only 72 hours prior to our appointment with Ohashi. Naturally we were blindsided, devastated, and confused with a million questions about how this could have happened. I spent 20 solid minutes talking to her assistant Dr. Josie trying to thoroughly explain Obi's medical history over the last 2 years as well as what we had been told by our primary vet (which was that he was perfectly healthy as far as they could tell), and that we were given no signs or indications that he had been sick or in any kind of pain. Dr. Josie appeared understanding and empathetic until she left and return with Ohashi and then she never spoke or looked at us directly in the eye again. It was cruel and unusual.

I then tried to reexplain everything to Ohashi but her English was so terrible it was like talking to an AI Chatbot and she never fully acknowledged or responded to a single thing I said to her in the 2 days we spent with her. Instead she spoke to us as if we had left our dog to suffer in pain for years on end and repeated statements such as "how long are you going to continue to make him suffer like this" as my husband and I sobbed begging her to listen to us and understand.

In addition to this, we clearly stated to Ohashi that Obi was having trouble walking on his hind legs. He had been taken for X-rays and when Ohashi came to speak with us she told us he was having trouble walking on his front legs. Again, we tried to explain that this was incorrect and we had not experienced this with him and she flat out told us we were wrong. AGAIN she was incapable of listening and understanding. Shortly after, they brought Obi back to us and he could barely walk on his front legs. We had never seen this before and it was clear he had been severely injured during the X-rays.

This was the last day Obi ever walked again. That night he became paralyzed. We 100% attribute this to how he was handled during the x-rays.

After he became paralyzed, Ohashi told us to come back and give him an infusion of medication that would help him walk again. This treatment cost $1200 and it wasn't until after he was given the treatment that we were told by Ohashi that it wouldn't work on him if the issue was neurological (versus due to his cancer). In Obi's final days, he suffered unnecessarily. We all did.

My French bulldog began having seizures 7 months ago, and after not getting much information from my own vet, I reached out to the Neurology Dept at VCA. I’m so grateful for this clinic! They’re not my regular veterinary hospital since my dog and I are based in the Bay Area, but they truly went above and beyond for us.

Both veterinarians made an incredibly stressful situation much more manageable. Their kindness, professionalism, and genuine care meant so much to me, and I’m so thankful we found this clinic when we needed help the most. I can’t recommend them enough.
Very nice people gives u the best options price wise
My cat receives the best service and care. The staff's really friendly and helpful. It's exactly what pet parents need during a stressful event with our fur babies.
Really solid care all around in an emergency, would pay top tier prices again to get this level of care.

Kimmy, Beatriz and the Emergency Veterinarian are Angels...my little guy of 18 years passed tragically and unexpectedly and he was beyond saving. I'm so grateful for the compassionate services we received. The ability to hold my baby boy one last time meant so much. Thank you...we're eternally grateful for your kindness.

I will NEVER. NEVER BRING AN ANIMAL HERE EVER AGAIN!!!

Brought my kitty in last year because she was having a hard time breathing. They took her back and didn’t actually see her for SIX HOURS. SHE GASPED FOR AIR. FOR SIX HOURS. I will never recommend or take any of my animals here again. My dog was not doing good and basically on his death bed. I was able to have my dog peacefully put down with a team who actually cares at the other facility (urgent care Burbank)
I will not recommend VCA and I hope that the receptionist knows that her interaction was horrible and to say what you did to me as you saw my dog in my arms. Exceptionally rude and adversarial. Do not recommend.

Do not recommend.
Stay away!

My cat has had severe fever symptoms twice in the last two weeks. During the first visit, I spent about $900 on testing and care, and the blood work came back normal. When the symptoms returned, the main recommendation was to repeat the same basic blood work again.

What frustrated me most was that I repeatedly asked a very simple question: "What are the names of the tests I can ask for, either here or somewhere else, to look for possible diseases or cancer?" I asked multiple times and never received a direct answer from the vet assistant. Instead, the conversation kept circling back to repeating the same blood work.

After already spending around $900, I expected more transparency and a clear explanation of what other diagnostic options might exist. The refusal or inability to provide the names of additional tests left me questioning the integrity of the recommendations I was being given. When the primary solution seemed to be paying for the same testing again, without answering basic questions about other available diagnostics, it created the impression that generating another bill was a higher priority than helping me make informed decisions about my cat's care.

I understand that diagnosing an illness can be difficult and that repeat testing may sometimes be necessary. However, pet owners deserve clear answers, honest communication, and a full discussion of available options. Unfortunately, that was not my experience.

I was very disappointed with my experience. Dr. Biggo told me my dog's mast cell tumor needed to be treated sooner rather than later because its growth could not be predicted, yet I was not informed during the consultation that Dr. Biggo was leaving town.

At my May 19 consultation, I specifically explained that I was having surgery myself on May 20 and asked whether my dog's surgery could be postponed for 2 weeks. Dr. Biggo recommended surgery sooner rather than later. Based on that recommendation, I moved forward with pre-operative testing on May 24 despite recovering from my own surgery.

Only after completing the pre-operative procedures was I informed that Dr. Biggo would be out of town and that the earliest surgery date available was June 17.

Because timing was a central part of our discussion, I believe Dr. Biggo's upcoming absence and inability to perform surgery for almost a month should have been disclosed from the beginning so I could make an informed decision about my dog's care.

I have only ever had a wonderful experience here. I have an older dog, almost 16 years old and while our primary vet is the brilliant Dr.Belding at VCA Chatoak - this office has been incredible multiple nights after hours for us. I am incredibly grateful for the kind staff and caring vets at this office. I trust them immensely and am forever thankful for many visits spent helping my senior dog.

After receiving a call from our regular veterinarian telling us we needed to take our dog to an emergency hospital immediately, I knew exactly where to go: Animal Specialty Group. Five years earlier, our dog had been treated in their Emergency Department and spent several days under their care. That experience left such a lasting impression on us that there was no question where we would turn during another crisis.
From the moment I called, we were shown kindness and urgency. The receptionist listened carefully, placed me on a brief hold, and then calmly told us to bring our dog in right away. In such a stressful moment, that compassion alone meant the world.
We were incredibly fortunate that our sweet dog came under the care of Dr. Zabalaga. My husband and I were overwhelmed with emotion and initially had different thoughts about our dog’s care; one of us hoping to do whatever it took to bring him home that same day because of his anxiety, while the other leaned toward a more cautious approach if hospitalization was truly in his best interest.
Dr. Zabalaga recognized this dynamic immediately and handled it with remarkable grace, empathy, and emotional intelligence. She gave both of us the space to express our concerns without ever feeling judged or dismissed. During one of the most stressful moments imaginable, she helped us come together as a team. We both felt heard, respected, and genuinely cared for.
What stood out most was her balance of honesty and compassion. She gave us a clear and truthful understanding of our dog’s condition while always keeping his comfort and quality of life at the center of the conversation. She patiently explained everything in detail, recommended additional testing, and helped us understand how the results would guide the best path forward. Once the results came in, she walked us through them thoroughly and thoughtfully, allowing us to make informed and confident decisions about our dog’s care.
Because of her expertise and guidance, we were able to bring our sweet little guy home the same day and begin the lifelong treatment plan he now needs.
We truly cannot speak highly enough about Dr. Zabalaga. Exceptional medical expertise is one thing, but pairing it with this level of empathy, communication, and human understanding is rare. In one of our family’s most emotional moments, she made us feel supported every step of the way. We will forever be grateful.
Absolutely amazing care. Extremely thorough and quick to get you in. Grateful to have such an amazing vet practice / emergency service close by

I want to thank the Animal Specialty Group for saving my cat, Coco. Their service was attentive and thoughtful, and I was extremely satisfied! Coco is nearly four years old and has always been healthy; however, for some unknown reason, she began vomiting immediately after eating. In the past, this would happen occasionally—perhaps once or twice—and she would recover quickly. But this time, she went three consecutive days without being able to keep down any food or even water.

Consequently, I researched numerous emergency clinics and ultimately decided to take Coco to this facility for treatment. I had also checked online reviews for the clinic beforehand, which left me feeling somewhat apprehensive—worried that the costs would be exorbitant or that the doctors might order unnecessary tests. Thus, with a heart full of anxiety and trepidation, I brought Coco to the Animal Specialty Group. As it turned out, I had chosen the perfect place.

The receptionist at the front desk communicated with me very politely; noticing that my English wasn't strong, she used a translation app on her phone to facilitate our conversation. After completing the check-in process, she promptly notified a specialist to take Coco in for treatment. The doctor—a lovely young woman whose name I unfortunately didn't catch—conducted a preliminary consultation with us. She analyzed several potential causes for Coco's vomiting-after-eating symptoms, outlined the diagnostic tests that might be required, and—after obtaining our consent—proceeded with the examination. Later, a male staff member came to inform us of the estimated tests and associated costs; once I had settled the payment, I simply waited. After a total wait of about four hours, we were able to take Coco home. A member of the medical staff provided us with detailed instructions on how to care for Coco at home, including specific precautions to observe, and then we headed home.

The entire visit went very smoothly; the diagnostic tests and billing items were clearly itemized, with absolutely no signs of unnecessary or inflated charges. I was thoroughly satisfied with the experience, and I would like to extend a special thank you to the young lady at the front desk who assisted us. She was incredibly patient and never made us feel unwelcome or like a burden despite my language barrier—she is truly so sweet! Thank again 🙏🙏

Although the cost was a bit high, it was acceptable, as my Coco does not have pet insurance. Should my beloved pet ever require emergency medical attention again, I would certainly return here for treatment. My sincere thanks go out to every member of the medical staff here.🙏🙏🥰🥰

Hey Monica! 😊 Thanks so much for taking the time to share your rating with us! We're so glad you chose to be part of the VCA Animal Specialty Group family. If we can ever offer our support, answer any questions, or offer additional assistance, please know we're always here for you to connect with by emailing us at VCAContactUs@vca.com.🐾
Staff is very helpful and accommodating. Drs are amazing . Very compassionate

We took our dog to VCA ASG when she stopped eating and drinking and was confused and disoriented.
We explained that she’d had her first ever dose of simparica and the symptoms started right after taking that medication.
I’d done some research and learned that the symptoms were a known side-effect of Solana, the active ingredient in simparica.
Dr. Manucci dismissed that information and instead diagnosed a brain tumor and recommended a neurological consult and an MRI. We did not take that recommendation. At that point the doctor was done with us. I asked one of the assistants to ask Dr. Manucci to call Zoetis, the manufacturer of simparica, and gave her the help line number. I could hear the doctor’s response to the request, “I can’t spend all day on the phone”  and she never did speak with them. So I called the help line and asked them to call VCA ASG and still Dr. Manucci would not speak with them. Another staff vet did. When she calked me to let me know she’d had a conversation with Zoetis her message to me was that everything would be inconclusive until we agreed to the neurologist consultation and an MRI (estimated cost $6,000). She didn’t offer that she’d confirmed that they were doing all that Zoetis recommended in this situation, so I asked her directly. She fumbled  but said of course they were.
Our dog spent 5 days at VCA ASG (total cost $11,000). When we decided to take her home they recommended a quality of life consult. They also reminded us yet again that we’d refused the MRI recommendation “for financial reasons.”Our dog is doing fine now. Three hours after getting her home she started eating and drinking on her own. It had been about a week since she ingested the simparica and she’d flushed out enough of it to feel and act normal again.
We are thrilled at how well she’d doing, and also absolutely certain we will never take her to VCA ASG again.
Expensive but great service!

Wonderful care and if you have the unfortunate need of taking your pet there, Wendy and the crew will take great care of you all.
You may be there for a while, but you can know they'll give you the same care they're giving others.

Will never return here. Questionable service and poor contact. Expensive procedures, then repeat procedures proposed again after they failed to make contact. No call back or follow up unless you initiate. Would not recommend.
Maria, thank you for taking the time to share this feedback! 💙 😊  …

Worst clinic ever.  Dont even think of going to this place.   They don’t care about your animal all they care about is running your bill up. My dog was there for 3 days they supposedly did all types of tests. Payed them more then 10 k in bills and brought my dog home with even worst symptoms then he had.  Go to Hillcrest they will take care of your animal the way you expect a veterinarian to take care of the animal. They are all lier’s there. Do not take your animal there you will not be happy.

Extremely attentive and communicative care. Before coming in, we called and were able to get advice directly from one of the vets on what we should do. Absolutely horrible!

It has been nearly 3 months since we said goodbye to our beloved fur baby, Pepper, at VCA ASG. We will never forget how gently he was taken care of in his last moments earth-side. They went above and beyond to explain next steps and ensure that we were able to get what we needed even when we thought it was too late.

Thank you for everything ASG- we appreciate it more than you know.

I had to bring my cat in for an emergency visit and the experience was genuinely great. Dr. Mason took so much time explaining the possible causes and treatment options, more thoroughly than most doctors I’ve seen for my own care. My cat was treated with real care and attention the entire time, and I really appreciated the follow up phone call afterward to check on how he was doing. The facility was clean, welcoming, and as comfortable as a vet environment can be. I left feeling confident that my cat was in very good hands

My dog was having frequent seizures and pressing her head against the wall and crying. I had spent the prior day at my vet where they did blood tests and an xray and given anti-seizure medication. Her condition got worse over the next day. I called ahead and was advised to bring her in to emergency. As soon as I walked in I was greeted and asked if that was Dolly. I said yes and she was immediately taken to the back to be evaluated. I thought I was going to be in for a long wait but was shortly called in to an exam room. I was quickly seen by Dr. Allehverdi. I can't say enough good about the treatment given to both me and Dolly by the doctor and the staff.
Manda, thank you for sharing your feedback!

Unfortunately, I had to euthanize my cat and it was absolutely so traumatic, at the end of my visit I went to pay at the front and Brianna J was very rude her attitude was extremely horrible especially that I just euthanized my cat, she wasn’t kind at all and the lack of compassion just blew my mind. I never usually write reviews but my encounter with just made me feel even worse.
Dr. Tom was amazing and Day at the front desk was extremely kind!

We brought our dog in during a medical crisis requesting humane euthanasia due to severe, escalating respiratory distress. I would not trust this clinic for end-of-life care.

My boy Urson is being treated by internal medicine here. We are so grateful because we found out through their recommended testing/endoscopy that he has GI small cell lymphoma (cancer). Dr. Rhonda Schulman is an expert and she takes the time to explain everything and answer all our questions. We’re very involved in his health and we appreciate the time the doctor takes to hear all our concerns regarding multivitamins and supplements in addition to his core treatment. Thank you for taking care of our boy!

This is my 2nd time at this location. The Dr. was very professional, examined my cat, and took the time to review what may cause his discomfort. The overall estimate wasn't cheap, but at least it felt more comfortable than other hospitals.

I always feel comfortable bringing my little girls to ASG when they need medical services .  The staff is always welcoming and I have confidence in the doctor staff .

Absolutely the best animal hospital ever!

Every single person at VCA Animal Hospital is amazing. From the front desk staff to the doctors, nurses, and even the security team — everyone is kind, professional, and truly cares about every pet and family that walks through the door.

They helped us so much and even saved our puppy’s life. The customer service is perfect, the employees are wonderful, and the doctors are caring and knowledgeable. You can feel how much love and effort they put into their work.

Thank you so much to the whole VCA team for being so awesome and for taking such great care of our puppy. We are forever grateful! ❤️🐾

I went to VCA last night at midnight with a lot of fear about the condition of my cat. every single person there was kind, empathetic and supportive. She answer my million questions very in depth and helped me understand what was going on. She spotted a few issues that I will now be able to address with my cats health going forward and helped make him comfortable as soon as she could. He is okay! and is now at home healing from the spine/tail pain he was experiencing.
Even the man who came to take my cat to the vet was very kind and empathetic.

I’ve been to cold vets office where I don’t feel like the staff really care that much about me or my cat. This place is the opposite. They even write the pets names on the room they are in with a little heart. (every single room I saw with a name had a heart)

The prices were definitely emergency room prices but not as bad as I thought they were going to be. and the women at the front even helped my find a coupon on the VCA website to help with the cost.

Thank you VCA for being so kind and supportive during a really hard night. I feel lucky that I live so close and will be using this place as my emergency vet if (god forbid) I ever need to again.
This place is fine. They aren’t going to really help you. Will charge you up the wall. Wish we hadn’t wasted our time with them. Probably could have saved my cat if I had known better.

We want to give our deepest thanks to Dr. Knieriemen. We never felt rushed, whether in person or on the phone, with Dr. Knieriemen consistently willing to answer as many questions as we had calmly, patiently and at length. We received multiple follow ups by phone from Dr. Knieriemen after our dog Georgia was discharged. Despite having to give us devastating news with lots of tears involved, Dr. Knieriemen had such an excellent bedside manner and made us feel truly cared for. Most of all - I just want to give the most glowing review of all. My dog HATES the vet, and will usually cower in the corner whenever being seen by one. We knew in that moment that Dr. Knieriemen is a true gem, even (and most importantly) in the eyes of our dog. Thank you for everything.

VCA Animal Specialty Group has taken care of so many of my pets. I have had a special relationship with them for many years and I know that I can always trust them to care for my pets. Most recently my Great Dane puppy Charlie ate something she shouldn’t have and needed surgery. I’m so thankful for the surgical team and all those that cared for her. I’m forever grateful for how they helped Charlie and my family.

Our beloved 5-year-old cat suddenly lost his appetite. We took him to his regular vet, who performed blood tests and found high ammonia levels. The vet suggested we take him to a specialized hospital, so we went to VSA Animal Hospital at 4641 Colorado Blvd, Los Angeles, CA 90039.

After five days, we made the painful decision to put him to sleep

According to staff dog has a rash and other animals were placed ahead even though the cost to be seen is the same and we have pet insurance.

We had to say goodbye to our incredible dog Hazel today. I recommend this location highly.

Dr. Sengewald saved our kitten, Baldwin, from what turned out to be a severe case of dry/ocular/neurological FIP. Very courteous and caring staff. Very professional. On time appointments. Very knowledgeable

Great staff and Dr. Collins was very calm and carrying towards my cat. Who doesn’t like anyone. Overall great experience and will recommend her to my family and friends.

Dr. Collins was the perfect match for us! Our dogs are apart of our family. Having someone being openly honest and truthful for us is what we needed. Would recommend her to anyone seeing the compassion she has.

Pup had a swollen nose from a bee sting but was taken care of swiftly and she was back to her happy self later that day. Thank you VCA for being so kind and helpful.

Huge thanks to Dr. Collins for the outstanding care and support she gave our family Rottweiler. I feel like the VCA completely price gouged me, and didn't even give him the surgery he needed. I told them I would take my cat to a different facility because at that point I was concerned about my cat and whether he was okay.
When my cat was returned to me, I didn't think about checking to see if he was dry. When I picked him up in the car to put on my lap he was so drenched that he soaked all the way through my clothes.

Never in my life have I experienced such caring and compassionate veterinary professionals. They treated our best guy like one of their own and when he lost his battle with cancer they wept with us and comforted us like we were family. They gave Benny a comfortable and dignified ending in our arms and let us stay with him as long as we wanted. I can’t imagine going through that experience without their guidance and care.
Glad this place is here! Was able to get my pup some help and the vet was very nice and informative.
Never got very far. Receptionist hung up on me. Definitely going somewhere else.

Bree answered the call.   She could not have been more rude.   Shocking to be greeted by someone that is rude, argumentative and constantly interrupting the conversation.   You would think that the receptionist at an emergency Vet would not answer the phone with more empathy and patience considering the next available appt for a dying pet is an ENTIRE MONTH AWAY.   Bree is in the wrong business.

Think twice about coming to this hospital unless it’s an absolute emergency and you have no other choice.

If it’s for a re-check of a procedure they performed, you’re likely to be a second class citizen with some disgruntled front desk staff who drum up excuses, sometimes insulting your intelligence, just to get you to sit down and wait your turn since you’re not an urgent case. (And they’ll tell you there are other dogs before you that are in worse condition. As if an open laceration that’s oozing pus from their inadequate suturing isn’t.)

Front desk staff (some) have sharp tongues, anre defensive, and are not as sensitive as they should be to your needs or emotional state.

Go to your regular vet if you can wait for a re-check on an open wound that was inadequately sutured by them to begin with.

Sure, it’s Memorial Day but why do you remind of the holiday, you’re understaffed,  and how unhappy you are that you’re working on a holiday? Life isn’t all we want it to be. Grow up.

As a team, work together instead of blaming people with sick animals who come to you for help. It’s immature and playing the victim doesn’t make VCA ASG a place I’d trust with my dog.

There are other emergency vet clinics. Consider them. They might even be less expensive, who knows.

Again, assess your situation and if you can wait to see your trusted primary vet, wait. Don’t put yourself through more of the unnecessary stress you already have with your sick pet.

I never thought I’d be back here so soon, but at 4 a.m. Tuesday morning, my dog suddenly yelped and went into cardiac arrest. She had no history of heart issues—just sudden heart failure. I rushed her to VCA Animal Specialty, and they took her to the back right away and did everything they could. Sadly, she had gone about 15 minutes without oxygen, and it was too late. My girl was gone.

The staff was incredibly kind and supportive. They let me sit with her for as long as I needed and treated her with such dignity and care. They held her remains until I could arrange a private cremation. A team member carefully brushed and clipped her hair, wrapped her gently in a soft bag (no trash bags here), and laid her in a small coffin adorned with flowers.

Losing her so suddenly was devastating, but the compassion and respect shown by the staff brought comfort during one of the hardest moments of my life. Again I am forever grateful.

A huge thank you to everyone at VCA for our experience with them. Our cat was experiencing an emergency around midnight, and we took him here hoping for the best. The staff were all so kind and helpful, despite him being very scared and thus not on his best behavior. They talked us through everything they needed to do and made a bad situation better. He made a full recovery thanks to their help. Plus, really appreciated that the waiting room had Harry Potter and Bob Ross videos playing to calm us down. Not cheap but what emergency vet is? Thank you for helping our boy when he needed it. ❤️

Unfortunately VCA is owned by private equity and seeks to extract as much money as possible from pet owners. Their prices are exorbitant. They quoted us over 12k for hospitalization just for them to see the specialist the next day to see if our dog might need surgery for his leg or not. Luckily we went to VSS in Orange County and ended up not needing surgery at all. The cost there was also half of what VCA quoted us for the same surgery. Do not recommend you come here.

Listen, going to the vet is an awful experience if your pet is sick and everything is undoubtably expensive. But, the vet’s assistant I worked with for my dog’s emergency room visit here today was the absolute worst. She was cold, rude, and honestly - I believe she kept my dog longer than was required. I watched everyone come and go for 5 hours and it turned out my dog just had a UTI, so there was no reason to keep him. When I asked when I could leave (the vet already said I was all set) around 12:30a I got no answers. I had to demand to retrieve my dog at 2am and the assistant finally came out. I’ve had better experiences when I’ve had appointments here, but the emergency experience was so brutal that I don’t know if I’ll ever return.

I should say, my dog has chronic illness so I’m used to vets and emergency rooms, sadly. None are good experiences, but usually the staff have good bedside manner. For the price you are paying, go to MASH or Access, at a minimum, they don’t hold your dog unnecessarily for hours on end.

Lastly, in my first interaction with the nurse assistant, I asked questions about the absurd bill ($800) and she seemed annoyed that I had questions. It was terrible from the start. BUT! The vet did answer my questions and listened so that’s good - but overall, still so frustrated with how I was treated.
At a rough time for our family VCA has gone above and beyond... The kindness and thoughtfulness has been so amazing.

Brought my dog in who was experiencing a range of odd symptoms, and they were very dismissive. The doctor came in to talk to us and she was clearly not briefed on what was going on, it seemed as though this was her first time even seeing my dog. We explained what was going on and the doctor did not give us any answers, and framed it as though my dog was totally fine. She left and someone else came it to give us a $2,000 estimate in various exams they could administer (no one ever gave us an answer on what was going on or what they recommended). We never saw the doctor again, but instead opted to leave and go elsewhere.
Turns out my dog had a double ear infection and a stroke.

Find a different place tot go. My dog had been cut above her eye on a Saturday night. There was no one in the waiting room at this vet group, but we were there nearly three hours anyway. Eventually, the vet told me my dog didn’t need stitches, so all they were going to do was sedate her, shave the area, give her a cone and antibiotics and send her home. The estimate was $815 to 1,000!!!! I was shocked. I usually go to VCA, which is somewhat pricey, but this was insane!!! In the end, I paid $400 for just the visit and the medications — The vet wouldn’t even clean the wound for that much. I’m disgusted — imagine paying $400 for a visit in which the vet won’t clean a small wound. Outrageous.

We had a middle of the night emergency and had to say goodbye to our sweet girl and the whole team approached us with kindness, compassion, and so supportive. They treated our sweet girl with love and mercy. I can’t express my gratitude for the team making a horrible situation a little bit easier. They were truly our light in a very dark night.

Setting the VCA aside and rating this hospital
1. Initial phone call requesting emergency care for my pug 5/5 stars
Automated part was clear and easy to understand.
Staff .member who answered my call was knowledgeable and polite
2. Reception.
Staff was knowledgeable and polite and immediately called for back staff to come up front to triage my dog who was going paralyzed that very second. Tech was great, took my dog to be assessed by the ER doctor immediately.
Waiting room was clean with a great coffee bar/ espresso area  large screen TV , ending machines

I showed up at 8:45 with my 1 year old pup. She has a cough and runny nose. It took 1 hour to get seen which was expected, however I was there for an additional 4 hours and all that happened was they took vitals and told me that they wanted to do crashed and blood work. Almost 4 hours later I was still sitting in the same little room, no updates given so we decided to leave and see our normal vet in 2 days.
So 5 hours, missed day of work and I got charged 240 dollars for a 5 hour wait and only vitals taken.
Total rip off and waste of time

Today I had to make the most heartbreaking decision of putting my Cashmere to sleep. The team at the front desk were very supportive and compassionate. The doctor that performed the procedure was very compassionate as well. It was quick and when he was finished he said "ok, she's asleep. Do you need more time? I can step out and come back when you are ready for me to take her. But please take as much time as you need." I loved the compassion and dignity that they showed us. ❤️

Absolutely a scam.
Took advantage of a young couple who just got a puppy.
Made us do a parvo test only because he is under 1 year old. Even with no symptoms

Brought our senior dog Sweet Pea in after cluster seizures which was terrifying and she never had before. We came in with no appointment and were attended to right away. It is expensive but they provide a high/low estimation for treatment before you pay the deposit. Dr Lombardi and team were very thorough with their assessment of SP and provided good documentation as it was overwhelming. I also find they did not push an MRI on us given sweet peas age. The front desk team were also so nice and it can’t be an easy job. I was/am happy with the care we’ve been given at this stressful and sad time.

The VCA team is incredible. Over the years, they’ve been with us through some of the most difficult moments, and their compassion and professionalism never falter. We’ve never felt pressured in our decisions, and the level of care they provide—especially during end-of-life situations—is remarkable.

When we’ve had to say goodbye to our pets, they ensure the process is as dignified and loving as possible. From giving us time to say goodbye to the way they prepare our pets for cremation, they handle everything with utmost care and respect. The flowers on the transport box are such a thoughtful touch, and they never use anything impersonal like trash bags for remains.

They even follow up with a heartfelt card, which is so meaningful during such a tough time. VCA is a true class act, and we can’t thank them enough for the care they’ve provided to our furry family members. If you’re looking for a veterinary practice that prioritizes compassion, respect, and professionalism, VCA is second to none.

VETS AT VCA ASG HAVE BEEN SUED FOR IMPROPER SUPERVISION OF INTERNS. I HAVE ALSO FILED A LAWSUIT.

If you're a pet parent who wants the best treatment possible for your pet in a time of crisis, I recommend going elsewhere. If you bring your pet here for emergency/critical care, IMHO you should expect
- to never speak with the vet who is making treatment decisions about your pet
- to have an intern with less than 3 months experience, who cannot make treatment decisions and says that they are tired, and have had a really long day, as the vet managing your pet's care
- that medical records will not be updated in a timely manner which may lead to missed doses of medication, treatment delays, poor treatment decisions, and possible complications
- you will likely never really know what happened to your pet, bc the records will not be thorough or accurate.

CONCERNS RE DR COLLINS, INTERNS, for every Pet Parent to be aware of before seeking emergency/critical care at VCA ASG.

We brought our dog in for emergency/critical care due to elevated kidney values.
- we asked repeatedly to speak with the "supervisor" Dr Collins - she never spoke to us
- we agreed on a treatment plan with intern Lombardo on Sunday am (at the time, we did not know she was an intern) - treatment plan was changed without our consent

- Again, we were told he was doing well and improving about 24 hours after admission. We came to visit him, and in our opinion (3 ppl), he was objectively worse than when he was admitted. He was struggling to breath. He was incredibly disoriented. We asked the front desk to page a doctor, and intern Lombardo came out and seemed (in my opinion) bewildered and unsure of what to do.

- when we asked for confirmation that he was being given his regular medication which reduces reflux we recall intern Lombardo saying that it was not given, b/c her supervisor decided on a different plan. When we requested that she give the medication we recall her saying that she could not, because Dr Collins was NOT in the hospital and she couldn't give him medication without Dr Collins approval. We asked her to call Dr Collins, we recall her saying she could not reach Dr. Collins.
- I called later that evening to confirm he'd been given his medication - the vet on duty indicated that ONCE AGAIN, HE WAS NOT GIVEN HIS MEDICATION AS AGREED and it was not written on his chart, so she would not give it to him. Intern Lombardo had not completed notes about treatment plan prior to leaving for the night.

- the following AM, Mister was put into oxygen as soon as Intern Lombardo arrived "as a precaution". It seems improbable that they just randomly put a dog in oxygen for no particular reason. Furthermore, when his pulse ox was taken after he had been in oxygen for some time, it was lower than normal (one can only imagine what it was before he was put on oxygen).

- I asked to see him (I recall I'd previously been told I could see him in the am), and was told I would have to wait until lunch time. After the agreed on time, a tech came to tell me that I would not be allowed to see him as agreed. Shortly after, I recall I was asked 3 times, by 3 different VCA employees, to update and sign a DNR.
- When I saw him later, I noticed his cone was tied so tightly, HIS CONE WAS RESTRICTING HIS BREATHING. An assistant checked the cone, and immediately removed it - he had aspirated on his cone. As soon as the cone was removed, he gasped for air, it was heartbreaking.

Mr. Mister was never the same after he returned home. He stopped using his buttons to communicate, he stopped barking for 2 months, he wouldn't go down stairs, and was very sensitive on his right side. Months later during an x-ray with another vet, we found he had multiple broken ribs likely due to trauma, which he did not have on admission to VCA.

Before bringing your pet here for emergency/critical care, read up on lawsuits against them.

My  dog Charlie was admitted to VCA Sunday morning, he had been throwing up all night and was unable to put weight on his legs. He was treated by
Dr Emily Coddon DVM.
We were told to pick Charlie up between 3-4 pm that the doctor was leaving at 4. I rushed from a conference in Orange County got there at 3:30: the doctor had gone home because "she didn't have enough patients"
I was greeted with a tech who didn't know a thing what was written on a piece of paper she handed -and tried to read to me. I was told that the doctor would call me after business hours on Monday.
I called on Monday and guess what? Doctor wasen't there. "She's more of a daytime doctor" they said.

I really appreciate their 24 hour emergency service. They are much more affordable than a lot of other places, especially when you are going there in the late hours/early morning. They were very accommodating and I feel like their entire staff (ESPECIALLY THE FRONT DESK PPL) are very friendly.

My cat urgently needed an E tube for feeding after her appetite was just too inconsistent to leave her to her own devices, and Dr. Alvarez here took great care of my baby! She was very knowledgeable and explained things to us about the care plan without talking down to us, and she really put us at ease during a stressful time. When we left my cat there overnight, we really felt she was in great hands, and the staff were all so patient with us. You can really tell they care about the animals here, and I would recommend it to anyone in a pet emergency.

Bonus: The bill for services was literally HALF of what we were quoted for the same services by another 24/7 emergency vet with specialties in Pasadena. So, so glad we chose to bring my cat here for her procedure even if it was a further drive.

I just want to express that this place did nothing for our dog. We came in because our dog was vomiting and had diarrhea. The pricing was outrageous. First of all, they tested him for things that were not a concern. Second, they did not provide to us any proof of the procedures done to our dog. They didn't even tell us what was wrong with him. They told us everything was normal and nothing was seen in the x-rays. They sent us home with prebiotic that I could of bought myself, canned food, and nothing else. Then, they put a bunch of fluids in him. The next day, our dog was pooping with blood, which he did not have. They charged us over $1500 and did nothing for my dog. This was a bad experience, and I really believe that all they want is money. Stay away from this place, I was just in a desperate moment, which they took advantage of. I called to get copy of his labs and x-rays and they did not like that very much, that they sounded rude when we asked for them. Please read the bad reviews before you make a decision to go to this place.
